newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ lender raises key mortgage rate to 10.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: NZ lender raises key mortgage rate to 10.5 pct.

text.p: New Zealand lender Countrywide Bank said on Wednesday it was raising its key variable mortgage rate to 10.5 percent from 8.95 percent.

The bank said its move, which it had clearly signalled last week, followed a sharp increase in the cost of wholesale funds highlighted by the 90-day bank bill rate surging from just over 7.0 percent in late June to over 8.50 percent in recent days.

Late last week several banks said they were reconsidering mortgage rate levels after the strong rise in the rates on short-dated money market securities, through which many of them source the funding for mortgage lending.

Other lenders, whose variable rates range from 8.25 to 8.95 percent, are widely expected to follow Countrywide's move up, although several do not have quite as high relative exposure to home loans within their total loan portfolios as Countrywide does.
"We have led the major banks down in the last three rate reductions," Countrywide managing director David Wolfenden said in a statement.
"It is disappointing for us to have to make this move, however we have been left with no alternative in view of the unexpected rise in wholesale rates," he added.
Countrywide is a unit of Bank of Scotland Plc.
